A 57-year-old man presents with a 3-week history of skin lesions on his lower extremities,
accompanied by fatigue and progressive numbness and weakness in his right hand. He denies
abdominal pain, cough, or shortness of breath. His medical history is notable for a past incarceration of
10 years and homelessness since his release last year. He has a history of intravenous drug use but
has been abstinent for the past 5 years. He is up-to-date on vaccinations. On examination, he is alert
and oriented, with a temperature of 38.1ºC (100.6ºF), pulse 74/min, respirations 14/min, and blood
pressure 133/89 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals palpable purpura on the lower extremities and
decreased muscle strength, reflexes, and sensation in the right upper extremity. Peripheral pulses are
intact bilaterally, and there is no pedal edema. Chest auscultation is unremarkable. Laboratory studies
